summary: Pre-Vote update required a model change (new pre-candidate state, Pre-Vote messages, a new elect() caller, changed tick/do_elect/become_following). The reference, MC, Trace and Update suites were updated; the prior harness was rebased; 17 fresh traces pass TLC trace validation with 12/12 negative controls rejected; two prior-model defects (empty-log comparison, leader lease on establishment) were repaired. Model checking found three update-introduced defects, all reproduced on the updated implementation through the public API: a timer Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect (MC-1), and two RaftCore panics in Candidate::grant_by when a completed or repeated round involves nodes outside the frozen quorum set (MC-2, MC-3). A documentation mismatch about Unreachable pre-vote responses (pre_vote.md) was noted as code review only.
validation_limits: All TLC campaigns are bounded (3 nodes, 2 in one hunt; terms <= 2-3; log index <= 3-4; bounded elections, pre-vote rounds, membership changes, crashes, drops, messages) and most BFS runs stopped at their time budget with states left on the queue (LIMITED_COVERAGE), followed by bounded simulation; no exhaustive pass or proof is claimed.

Membership learners and follower-side membership changes are not modelled; the non-voter election outcome is a nondeterministic union, and the follower variant of MC-3 is covered only by source analysis.
The engine-level harness captures the frozen candidate/pre-candidate quorum through the effective membership (private field); no traced scenario changes membership after a round starts.
Timer, lease and RPC-timeout behaviour are abstracted as enablement nondeterminism; their effect is exercised only by the runtime reproductions.
MC-1's runtime reproduction needs timing assistance (slow vote persistence emulated in the test store plus RPC hook delays); a pure black-box Level-0 attempt did not hit the window.
Old-revision controls are not runnable because the Pre-Vote API does not exist in the old revision; attribution to the update rests on source comparison.
External issue trackers were not consulted (blinded run); novelty is NEW with respect to the supplied tree only.

findings.title: Timer-started Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect
findings.cause: handle_tick_election starts a Pre-Vote round for a Candidate whose election timed out; establish_leader/become_leader do not clear pre_candidate, and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on the round's quorum without re-checking role or vote.
findings.trigger: With enable_pre_vote, a candidate's real election outlives its election timeout (e.g. slow vote persistence); the timer starts a Pre-Vote round at term+1; the real quorum then makes it Leader; the round's quorum arrives afterwards.
findings.consequence: The established leader starts a new election at term+1 without any external request or higher term: leadership is abandoned and the term inflates; the stale Leader object (vote behind state.vote) trips the try_leader_handler assertion (RaftCore panic in debug builds) and, in release builds, the cluster stayed leaderless with the term inflating.

premises: Pre-Vote is enabled (Config::enable_pre_vote or runtime toggle) and the cluster has more than one voter.
A candidate's real election can complete after its election timer fired but before the vote RPC timeout (election_timeout_min).
Only do_elect and become_following clear pre_candidate.
The PreVoteResponse runtime gate checks only pre_candidate presence and leader-id equality.

findings.title: Completed Pre-Vote round elects a node that left the voters; its self-grant panics RaftCore
findings.cause: handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() without the is_voter check performed by every old elect() caller; do_elect then builds a candidate over voters that exclude the node and the runtime's local self-grant reaches Candidate::grant_by, whose expect panics.
findings.trigger: A Pre-Vote round is in flight on a leader (explicit trigger().elect(true), or a stale timer round from MC-1) while the leader removes itself from the voters (kept as learner); the round's grants arrive after the change.
findings.consequence: RaftCore panics ('target not in quorum set') and the node stops serving (Fatal::Panicked), in debug and release builds.

premises: A Pre-Vote round can be in flight on a leader (explicit trigger accepts any voter; MC-1 keeps timer rounds).
A leader may remove itself from the voters while retained as learner and keeps running until it steps down.
The runtime sends a local granted VoteResponse after every non-committed SaveVote.

findings.title: Repeated Pre-Vote round at the same hypothetical vote counts a delayed grant from a removed node; RaftCore panics
findings.cause: Rounds started at an unchanged vote probe the same (term+1, self); the PreVoteResponse gate correlates by leader id only, and handle_pre_vote_resp calls grant_by for any granted response, which panics for a node outside the new round's quorum set.
findings.trigger: Round A over {0,1,2}; node 1's grant is delayed; node 1 is removed from the voters; round B is started at the same vote over {0,2}; node 1's round-A grant arrives within the RPC timeout.
findings.consequence: RaftCore panics ('target not in quorum set') and the node stops serving, in debug and release builds.

premises: Two Pre-Vote rounds can be started at an unchanged vote (explicit triggers, or timer re-issue).
A membership change can remove a responder between the rounds.
Vote/pre-vote RPC responses can arrive up to election_timeout_min after sending.
